question: Evaluate $\int_0^\pi \sin^3 x dx$ using the reduction formula or trigonometric identities.
explanation:
Use the identity $\sin^3 x = \sin x(1-\cos^2 x)$.

So $\sin^3 x = \sin x - \sin x\cos^2 x$.

Let $I = \int_0^{\pi} \sin^3 x dx = \int_0^{\pi} \sin x dx - \int_0^{\pi} \sin x\cos^2 x dx$.

First integral: $\int_0^{\pi} \sin x dx = [-\cos x]_0^{\pi} = 2$.

Let $J = \int_0^{\pi} \sin x\cos^2 x dx$.

Put $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x dx$. Limits change from $1$ to $-1$.

Thus $J = \int_{-1}^{1} u^2 du = [u^3/3]_{-1}^{1} = 2/3$.

Therefore $I = 2 - 2/3 = 4/3$.
